blocks.text: The curse takes effect immediately as the Nawab writhes in unbearable urinary agony and finds relief nowhere. Neither posture, clerical recitation, nor established Muslim holy men can ease the torment that has seized him.

His suffering grows more terrifying because he begins to imagine The spirits of martyred Singhs closing in around him with weapons drawn. What had looked like a worldly illness is now understood as a visitation tied directly to Bhai Taru Singh's words.
By the end of the page, the Nawab's confidence in his own religious world has failed. Desperation begins pushing him toward the very Khalsa he had tried to crush.
